The *Gahapatijātaka* (Ja 199), titled *The Householder* in English, is a narrative discourse in the Pali *Jātaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the traditional framing narrative, the Buddha recounted the story during his stay at Jetavana concerning a backsliding monk (*ukkaṇṭhita bhikkhu*) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. Observing that womankind cannot easily be kept upright and will invariably err and deceive their husbands (*mātugāmo nāma arakkhiyo, pāpaṁ katvā yena ten' upāyena sāmikaṁ vañceti yevā*), the Buddha introduced the tale of the past (*atītaṁ āhari*), which opens with the verse phrase *Ubhayam me na khamati* ("I like not this") [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879].

In terms of text reuse, automated analysis by DharmaNexus records four internal matching passages (totaling 351 characters) shared with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (*Dutiyo bhāgo*), the longest segment pairing spanning §0.4–2.6 of the text and §827–832 of the commentary with a similarity of 0.91 [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral lists four modern translations across four languages, but records no external parallels; likewise, DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language alignments with a score of 10 or higher [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
